conditions, while the function carrier supplies Mathlib's product measurable space.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.IsFamilyMassPartition
definitions.body: (∀ i, 0 ≤ eta i) ∧ Antitone eta ∧ Summable eta ∧ (∑' i, eta i) ≤ 1
definitions.docstring: The infinite-simplex conditions for macroscopic descendant-family fractions.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.collisionMass
definitions.docstring: Pair-collision mass `σ(η) = ∑ᵢ ηᵢ²`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.MarkedMassPartition
definitions.docstring: A successful event records every macroscopic family fraction and its front displacement.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.xiMeasure
definitions.body:
Measure.map Prod.fst
    (ν.withDensity fun mark ↦ ENNReal.ofReal (collisionMass mark.1))
definitions.docstring:
The genealogy measure `Ξ(dη) = σ(η) ν(dη, ℝ)`, implemented by weighting the marked event
intensity by collision mass and projecting away the response mark.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.HasFiniteCollisionIntensity
definitions.docstring: The exact local-finiteness hypothesis for genealogy at every fixed sample size.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.samplePartitionChangeRateBound
definitions.docstring: Union-bound rate controlling every event that can change a sample of `n` ancestral blocks.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.addKingmanComponent
definitions.docstring: Add an independent Kingman binary-merger component at the dust point.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.xiSpeedTiltWeight
definitions.docstring: Exponential front-response weight for a marked mass partition.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.speedTiltedXiMeasure
definitions.body:
Measure.map Prod.fst
    (ν.withDensity fun mark ↦
      ENNReal.ofReal (collisionMass mark.1 * xiSpeedTiltWeight theta mark))
definitions.docstring:
The full conditioned genealogy formula
`Ξθ(dη) = σ(η) ∫ exp(-θr) ν(dη,dr)`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.oneFamilyMassPartition
definitions.body: fun i ↦ if i = 0 then x else 0
definitions.docstring: Embed a one-family event into the countable mass-partition space.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.totalFamilyFraction
definitions.docstring:
Total population fraction reached by all successful families in one breakout.  A front
trajectory sees this scalar but not how it is partitioned among independent origins.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.paintboxWeight
definitions.docstring:
Probability that a specified pair of ancestral blocks lands in the same family at a breakout
with mass partition `η`.  This is `σ(η) = ∑ᵢ ηᵢ²`, and it is the only thing the genealogy sees
about the partition at the pairwise level.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.disjointPairMergeProbability
definitions.body: 3 * ∑ i, ∑ j, if i = j then 0 else η i ^ 2 * η j ^ 2
definitions.docstring:
Probability that four specified ancestral blocks merge as two disjoint pairs into two
*distinct* families.  The factor three counts the pairings of four blocks; the ordered sum over
`i ≠ j` supplies the two families.

This event is the signature of a genuine Ξ-coalescent.  A Λ-coalescent has one family per
breakout and therefore assigns it probability zero.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.HasTwoPositiveFamilies
definitions.body: ∃ i j, i ≠ j ∧ 0 < η i ∧ 0 < η j
definitions.docstring:
A mass partition has genuine simultaneous-family structure exactly when two distinct
families carry positive mass.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.boundaryTiltMass
definitions.docstring:
Exponential mass of the binary one-step boundary transform.  With physical log-mgf
`logMgf`, critical parameter `criticalParameter`, and critical speed `criticalSpeed`, this is
`2 exp(-t⋆v⋆ + Λ(t⋆))`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.boundaryTiltCenteredFirstMoment
definitions.docstring:
Centered first derivative of the transformed one-step mass.  This is the scalar factor left
after differentiating the log-mgf, and is the quantity in the derivative boundary equation.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.derivativeSubtreeContribution
definitions.docstring:
Finite-generation derivative contribution of one stopping-line subtree.  `basePotential`
is the transformed position of its root; `additiveMass` and `derivativeMass` are the two
descendant martingales measured relative to that root.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.selectedPioneerFlux
definitions.docstring: Reproductive-value flux through a finite selected stopping line.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.paretoExceedanceMass
definitions.docstring:
Exact Pareto first-order exceedance mass contributed by a vertex of normalized weight `q`.
The derivative-martingale input says the true tail is asymptotic to this chart.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.distinctPairExceedanceMass
definitions.signature: {Pioneer : Type*} [Fintype Pioneer] [DecidableEq Pioneer] (mass : Pioneer → ℝ) : ℝ
definitions.body:
∑ first, ∑ second,
    if first = second then 0 else mass first * mass second
definitions.docstring: Ordered distinct-pioneer factorial mass for two exceedances.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.IsSelectedFluxDecomposition
definitions.body: ∀ index, exogenousFlux index = selectedFlux index + prunedFlux index
definitions.docstring:
An exogenous full-tree flux decomposes into the flux retained by selection and the flux
pruned before the stopping line.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.pioneerWeightFraction
definitions.docstring: Population fraction reached by a pioneer of reproductive weight `w`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.pioneerWeightDisplacement
definitions.docstring: Front displacement produced by a pioneer of reproductive weight `w`, at rate constant `γ`.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.amplitudeFront
definitions.docstring:
Real-valued front coordinate obtained from reproductive amplitude.  Unlike a literal
particle quantile, this coordinate remains continuous for lattice displacement laws.

definitions.name: Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.HasCommonProfileRelaxation
definitions.signature: (conversion backgroundAmplitude pioneerAmplitude backgroundCount pioneerCount : ℝ) : Prop
definitions.body:
backgroundAmplitude = conversion * backgroundCount ∧
    pioneerAmplitude = conversion * pioneerCount
definitions.docstring:
Both colours have relaxed to the same spatial profile when one conversion factor maps their
particle counts to their reproductive amplitudes.

hypotheses: HasCommonProfileRelaxation conversion backgroundAmplitude pioneerAmplitude backgroundCount pioneerCount

Descent.Blindness.XiFromMarks.countFract: HasCommonProfileRelaxation conversion backgroundAmplitude pioneerAmplitude backgroundCount pioneerCount

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.expectedNumClasses
definitions.docstring:
`E(K_n)`, the expected number of distinct alleles in a sample of `n` under the
infinite-alleles model with scaled mutation rate `θ`.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  `K_n` is the sum of the `n` indicators "the `i`-th sample member
starts a new class", whose means `seating_new_class_prob` computes off the Ewens weights, and
expectation is linear.  What is ASSUMED is the infinite-alleles convention itself -- every
mutation produces an allele never seen before -- which is K-G's model on p.33 and is a
statement about the marker, not the population.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.bertrandTerm
definitions.body: if n ≤ 1 then 1 else 1 / ((n : ℝ) * Real.log n)
definitions.docstring:
`1/(n log n)`, set to `1` below `n = 2` so that it is antitone on the positives -- which
is what the condensation test requires and what `1/(n log n)` on its own is not.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.bsRate
definitions.docstring:
The Bolthausen-Sznitman decrease rate, `γ_b = b(H_b - 1)`, as a function.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  `ComingDownCriterion.bolthausenSznitman_decrease_term` computes
each merger's contribution and `sum_bolthausenSznitman_rate` sums them.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.betaFn
definitions.body: Gamma a * Gamma b / Gamma (a + b)
definitions.docstring: The Beta function, `B(a,b) = Γ(a)Γ(b)/Γ(a+b)`.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.betaCoalescentRate
definitions.body: betaFn ((k : ℝ) - alpha) ((b : ℝ) - (k : ℝ) + alpha)
definitions.docstring:
**The Beta-coalescent's merger rates**, `Λ = Beta(2-α, α)`.

Empirical status: THIS IS THE MODEL, and a substantive one: Schweinsberg (2003) derives it
from offspring numbers with a heavy tail of index `α`, so choosing it is choosing a
reproduction mechanism, not a convention.  Whether a population has such a tail is the
empirical question, and `Descent.Blindness.MultipleMergerBlindness` records which statistics
could tell.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.collisionQuadruples
definitions.signature: (k : ℕ) : Finset (Fin k × Fin k × Fin k × Fin k)
definitions.ret_type: Finset (Fin k × Fin k × Fin k × Fin k)
definitions.docstring:
The quadruples a union bound must range over: two pairs, each a genuine pair, and
distinct as unordered pairs.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.blockTransition
definitions.body:
((Finset.univ.filter fun f : Fin k → Fin N ↦ (Finset.univ.image f).card = j).card : ℝ)
    / (N : ℝ) ^ k
definitions.docstring:
The one-generation block-count transition probability: from `k` lineages to `j`, counted
as the share of parent maps whose image has exactly `j` elements.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is a count over `WrightFisher.parentAssignment`'s sample space
divided by its size, which is that event's probability under the uniform law -- the same
reading `WrightFisher.noCoalescenceProb_eq_card_ratio` makes of the diagonal.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.blockMatrix
definitions.body: fun k j ↦ blockTransition N k j
definitions.docstring: The one-generation block-count operator, indexed by lineage count.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.blockGenerator
definitions.body:
fun k j ↦ if (j : ℕ) = (k : ℕ) then -deathRate k
    else if (j : ℕ) + 1 = (k : ℕ) then deathRate k else 0
definitions.docstring:
The coalescent's generator on lineage counts: `-d_k` on the diagonal and `d_k` one step
down, which is K-G (2.10) with `q_{ξη}` summed over the covers of a `k`-block state.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.blockStochastic
definitions.docstring:
**The stochastic matrix `Q` factors through**, `S = 1 + Q/d_n`.

Uniformisation: divide the generator by the largest exit rate and add the identity.  Every
entry is then non-negative -- the diagonal because `d_k ≤ d_n`, the subdiagonal because
`d_k ≥ 0` -- and each row still sums to one, because `Q`'s rows sum to zero.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.blockOperator
definitions.body: if N = 0 then 1 else blockMatrix n N
definitions.docstring:
**The one-generation operator**, extended by the identity at `N = 0` so that it is a
contraction for every `N`.  The limit is taken along `N → ∞`, so the value there is inert.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.harmonicSum
definitions.docstring:
`a_m = Σ_{i=1}^{m} i⁻¹`, Watterson's constant, as a real-valued sum.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a finite sum of reciprocals.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.expectedSegmentLength
definitions.docstring:
The expected branch length contributed by the phase with `k` lineages alive: the lineage
count times the mean holding time.

Empirical status: DERIVED, not posited.  The factor `k` is the number of lineages, i.e. the
block count `|R_t|` of `Descent.Coalescent.StateSpace.blocks`; the factor `d_k⁻¹` is the mean
of K-C (1.7)'s exponential holding time, computed in
`Descent.Coalescent.HoldingTime`.  Neither is introduced here.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.expectedTotalBranchLength
definitions.docstring:
`E(L_n)`, the expected total branch length of the `n`-coalescent tree: summed over the
`n - 1` phases the block count passes through, exactly as `Rates.meanTransitTime` sums the
same phases without the lineage-count weight.

Empirical status: DERIVED, not posited -- it is `Σ_k k · d_k⁻¹` with both factors supplied
elsewhere; see `expectedSegmentLength`.  In generations, multiply by `2 N_e`, the factor
`Descent.Program.Conventions.coalescentTimeScale` fixes.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.comesDownFromInfinity
definitions.docstring:
**Schweinsberg's condition.**  The block count comes down from infinity when the
reciprocal decrease rates are summable: the time to descend through every level is a
convergent sum, so infinitely many levels are passed in finite time.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a summability condition on a sequence of
rates; whether a population's genealogy has those rates is the empirical question, and
`Descent.Blindness.MultipleMergerBlindness` records which statistics could tell.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.descentCurve
definitions.docstring:
Aldous's descent curve `n(t) = 2/t`: the deterministic number of ancestral lineages at
time `t` in a Kingman coalescent started from infinitely many.

Empirical status: DERIVED, with one approximation named.  It is the solution of
`n' = -n²/2`, and `n²/2` is `deathRate` with `n(n-1)` replaced by `n²`.  That replacement is
the only inexactness, and `descentCurve_at_entranceTime` measures it: the curve lands one
lineage below the exact mean entrance time's index, which is precisely the dropped `-n`.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.cutBase
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (η : ER n) (c : Quotient η) : Finset (Fin n)
definitions.docstring:
The class of `c`, with its representative deleted: the `λ_c - 1` elements a cut set of
`c` is a nonempty subset of.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.cutClass
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (η : ER n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Quotient η
definitions.body:
if h : S.Nonempty then Quotient.mk η h.choose
  else Quotient.mk η ⟨0, Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (NeZero.ne n)⟩
definitions.docstring: Every cut set determines the class it cuts.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.IsCutSet
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (η : ER n) (S : Finset (Fin n)) : Prop
definitions.body: S.Nonempty ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, ∀ y ∈ S, η.r x y) ∧ (∀ x ∈ S, (Quotient.mk η x).out ∉ S)
definitions.docstring:
**A cut set.**  Nonempty, contained in a single class, and omitting that class's
canonical representative -- the last condition being what names each cut once instead of
twice.

hypotheses: splitBy η S = splitBy η T

Descent.Coalescent.splitBy_injective_on_: splitBy η S = splitBy η T

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.classFinset
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (η : ER n) (x : Fin n) : Finset (Fin n)
definitions.body: Finset.univ.filter fun y => η.r y x
definitions.docstring: The class of `x`, as a `Finset`.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.decreaseRate
definitions.body: ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 b, ((k : ℝ) - 1) * (b.choose k : ℝ) * lam b k
definitions.docstring:
**Schweinsberg's rate.**  The expected rate at which the block count DECREASES: each
`k`-fold merger destroys `k - 1` blocks, and there are `C(b,k)` sets of `k` to merge.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a weighted sum of the family's rates; which
rates a population has is the empirical question, and `Descent.Blindness.MultipleMergerBlindness`
records which statistics could tell.

hypotheses: ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → 0 < decreaseRate lam b
∀ i j : ℕ, 2 ≤ i → i ≤ j → decreaseRate lam i ≤ decreaseRate lam j
∀ b k : ℕ, 0 ≤ p b k
∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 b, p b k = 1
∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 b, ((k : ℝ
∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → h b = 1 / lamb b + ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 b, p b k * h (b - k + 1

Descent.Coalescent.schweinsberg_comesDow: ∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → 0 < decreaseRate lam b
∀ i j : ℕ, 2 ≤ i → i ≤ j → decreaseRate lam i ≤ decreaseRate lam j
∀ b k : ℕ, 0 ≤ p b k
∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 b, p b k = 1
∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 b, ((k : ℝ
∀ b : ℕ, 2 ≤ b → h b = 1 / lamb b + ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 b, p b k * h (b - k + 1

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.meanDescentTime
definitions.docstring:
The mean time for a block count to descend from infinity to level `b`, when it leaves
level `k` at rate `γ_k`: the sum of the mean sojourns.

Empirical status: DERIVED given the rates.  Each summand is the mean of an exponential of
rate `γ_k`, which `Descent.Coalescent.HoldingTime.integral_id_mul_holdDensity` computes from
K-C (1.7)'s density.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.diffusionOnPow
definitions.docstring:
The Wright-Fisher diffusion's generator acting on the monomial `xⁿ`, written out: the
diffusion coefficient `½x(1-x)` times the second derivative `n(n-1)x^{n-2}`.  The exponent is
written `m + 2` so that `n - 2` is a genuine natural number and no truncated subtraction can
hide in the statement.

Empirical status: THIS IS THE MODEL.  `½x(1-x)` is the Wright-Fisher diffusion's variance
term -- binomial sampling variance `x(1-x)/N` per generation, rescaled by `N` generations --
and asserting it of a population is asserting neutrality and constant size.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.coalescentOnPow
definitions.docstring:
The coalescent's block-count generator acting on the same monomial: at rate `d_n` the
lineage count drops from `n` to `n - 1`, changing `xⁿ` to `x^{n-1}`.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  `deathRate` is a cardinality of the state space
(`Descent.Coalescent.StateSpace.card_covers_eq_deathRate`), and the jump is to a state with one fewer block, which is K-C (1.4).

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.encode
definitions.docstring: **K-C section 3: `𝓔` as a subset of `2^{ℕ×ℕ}`.**

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.holdProduct
definitions.signature: (γ : ℕ → ℝ) (hγ : ∀ k, 0 < γ (k + 2)) : Measure (ℕ → ℝ)
definitions.body:
haveI : ∀ k : ℕ, IsProbabilityMeasure (holdMeasure (γ (k + 2))) := fun k ↦
    holdMeasure_isProbabilityMeasure (hγ k)
  Measure.infinitePi (fun k : ℕ ↦ holdMeasure (γ (k + 2)))
definitions.docstring: The clock: one holding time per level, independent, at that level's rate.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.ewensWeight
definitions.body: θ ^ (blocks ξ - 1) * ∏ c : Quotient ξ, (((classSize ξ c - 1)! : ℕ) : ℝ)
definitions.docstring: The Ewens weight of K-G (3.8), stripped of its normalising denominator.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.extendMap
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (ξ : ER n) (o : Option (Quotient ξ)) : Fin (n + 1) → Option (Quotient ξ)
definitions.body: fun x => if h : (x : ℕ) < n then some (Quotient.mk ξ ⟨x, h⟩) else o
definitions.docstring:
Where the extension sends each element: an existing class for the first `n`, and the
choice `o` for the new one.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.extend
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (ξ : ER n) (o : Option (Quotient ξ)) : ER (n + 1)
definitions.docstring:
**Seat the `(n+1)`-th sample.**  `extend ξ (some c)` puts it in class `c`; `extend ξ none`
gives it a class of its own.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  A construction of relations on `n+1` elements
from relations on `n`.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.classSize
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (ξ : ER n) (c : Quotient ξ) : ℕ
definitions.body: (Finset.univ.filter fun x : Fin n => Quotient.mk ξ x = c).card
definitions.docstring: `λ_c`, the size of a class.  Kingman's `λ` in K-C (2.3) and K-G (3.8).

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.familySize
definitions.signature: {N : ℕ} (f : Fin N → Fin N) (j : Fin N) : ℕ
definitions.docstring:
`ν_j`, the number of children of individual `j` under the pedigree map `f`.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is the cardinality of a fibre: "how many
offspring have `j` as their parent", written down.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.sameParentCount
definitions.signature: {N : ℕ} (f : Fin N → Fin N) : ℕ
definitions.body: ∑ a, ((univ.filter fun b ↦ f b = f a).card - 1)
definitions.docstring:
The number of ORDERED pairs of distinct individuals sharing a parent, counted from the
offspring side: for each `a`, the number of others in its sibship.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a count on a given pedigree.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.pairCoalescenceProb
definitions.docstring:
**K-G p.35: `p = Var(ν₁)/(N-1)`.**  The one-generation pair-coalescence probability of a
Cannings model with mean-one family size whose second factorial moment is `v`.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is `sameParentCount_eq_sum_familySize` divided by the number
of ordered pairs and simplified; `pairCoalescenceProb_eq_ratio` is that statement.  What is
empirical is the value of `v` for a given species, which is a measurement of fertility
variance and not of population size.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.wrightFisherSecondFactorialMoment
definitions.docstring:
Wright-Fisher's second factorial moment: `ν` is binomial `(N, 1/N)`, so
`E ν(ν-1) = N(N-1)/N² = (N-1)/N`, and its variance is `1 - 1/N`, which tends to the `σ² = 1`
K-G (4.2) uses for the Wright-Fisher time scale.

Empirical status: THIS IS THE MODEL -- it is the second moment of the family size under
`WrightFisher.parentAssignment`, i.e. a property of uniform independent parent choice, not
of any population.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.neutralFixation
definitions.docstring:
The neutral fixation probability: an allele at frequency `x` fixes with probability `x`.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is the function the neutral generator annihilates with the
right boundary values, which `neutralFixation_generator_eq_zero` proves.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.selectedFixation
definitions.docstring:
**Kimura (1962).**  The probability that an allele with scaled selection coefficient
`α = 4Nₑs`, currently at frequency `x`, eventually fixes.

Empirical status: DERIVED, given the model.  It is the solution of `L u = 0` with `u(0) = 0`
and `u(1) = 1` for the generator with a selective drift term, and
`selectedFixation_generator_eq_zero` is that verification.  What is ASSUMED is the diffusion
with drift `½α x(1-x)` -- genic selection, no dominance, constant size -- which is a model of
a population and not a consequence of one.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.selectedFixationDeriv
definitions.docstring:
The first derivative of Kimura's formula, named so the generator identity can be stated
as algebra.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.selectedFixationDeriv2
definitions.docstring: The second derivative, likewise.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.branchSurvival
definitions.docstring:
The probability that a sampled pair fails to coalesce within an internal branch of length
`T`: the `d_2 = 1` exponential survival of K-C (1.7).

Empirical status: DERIVED.  It is the survival function of the holding time in a two-block
state, whose rate is `Rates.deathRate 2 = 1` and whose density
`Descent.Coalescent.HoldingTime.holdDensity` supplies.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.discordanceProb
definitions.docstring:
**`P(gene tree ≠ species tree) = (2/3)e^{-T}`.**  The product of the two factors above:
the pair must fail to sort in the branch, and then must fail to sort correctly by chance.

Empirical status: DERIVED.  Both factors are the corpus's own -- the exponential from the
rate ladder, the `2/3` from the jump chain -- and this multiplies them.  What is ASSUMED is
that the three populations are related by a strict tree with no gene flow: with migration the
two events are not independent and the formula is not this one.  That is the standard
confound in the empirical literature, and `Descent.Coalescent.Structured` is where the corpus
keeps migration.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.prodUpTo
definitions.signature: {M : Type*} [Monoid M] (A : ℕ → M) : ℕ → M
definitions.body:
| 0 => 1
  | r + 1 => prodUpTo A r * A r
definitions.docstring:
The ordered product `A₀ A₁ ⋯ A_{r-1}`.  Written by recursion because the factors do not
commute, so a `Finset` product would be the wrong object.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.holdDensity
definitions.body: if 0 < t then ENNReal.ofReal (d * Real.exp (-(d * t))) else 0
definitions.docstring:
K-C (1.7): the sojourn density in a state with death rate `d`, as a density against
Lebesgue measure.  Zero on `t ≤ 0` -- a sojourn is positive.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.holdMeasure
definitions.docstring: K-C (1.7) as a measure.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.blockHoldMeasure
definitions.docstring:
**Kingman's clock, at the rate a `k`-block state carries.**  K-C (1.7)'s `d_k` is
`Descent.Coalescent.Rates.deathRate`, which `Descent.Coalescent.StateSpace.card_covers`
identifies as the number of covers -- so the clock's rate is the number of pairs of lineages
that could merge, which is the whole content of the coalescent's timing.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.coalescentLawExp
definitions.signature: (n k m : ℕ) (rate : ℕ) : Measure (List (ER n) × (Fin m → ℝ))
definitions.docstring:
**K-G section 6's temporal coupling at finite `n`, with nothing left as a parameter.**
The jump chain of `Descent.Coalescent.Trajectory`, coupled to independent copies of
Kingman's own clock.  Independence is arranged, as it is in K-C Theorem 3 -- see
`Descent.Coalescent.Law` for why that is the honest description and what it does not
settle.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is a coupling: `Descent.Coalescent.Trajectory`'s
jump chain paired with independent copies of `blockHoldMeasure`.  Constructing a joint law
whose marginals are two given objects asserts nothing about a population -- what it asserts
is about the two objects, and `Descent.Coalescent.Law` states exactly what the independence
does and does not settle.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.jumpProb
definitions.docstring:
The probability the jump chain assigns to each individual cover of a `k`-block state:
`q_{ξη}/q_ξ = 1/d_k`.  K-C (2.2).

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.jumpCoeff
definitions.docstring: The factorial prefactor of K-C (2.3).

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.absoluteProb
definitions.body: jumpCoeff n k * (((lam.map Nat.factorial).prod : ℕ) : ℝ)
definitions.docstring:
**K-C (2.3) itself**, as a function of the class sizes: the absolute probability that
the jump chain, having reached `k` blocks, is at a state whose classes have the given sizes.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is Kingman's formula, written down; what is
proved below is that it satisfies the recursion its proof requires.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.jumpLaw
definitions.body: if h : 2 ≤ blocks ξ then (jumpStep ξ h).map Subtype.val else PMF.pure ξ
definitions.docstring:
The one-step law of the jump chain as a mass function on the whole state space: uniform
on the covers when there is anywhere to go, and the point mass otherwise.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.jumpKernel
definitions.signature: (n : ℕ) : Kernel (ER n) (ER n) where toFun ξ
definitions.ret_type: Kernel (ER n) (ER n) where toFun ξ
definitions.docstring:
**The jump chain of the `n`-coalescent as a Markov kernel on `𝓔ₙ`.**

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  The transition law is forced by K-C (1.3)'s unit
rates and the cover count (`jumpStep_apply_eq_jumpProb`); the only free choice is what an
absorbed chain does, and `jumpKernel_absorbing` records the convention taken.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.IsConsistentRates
definitions.body: ∀ b k : ℕ, 2 ≤ k → k ≤ b → lam b k = lam (b + 1) k + lam (b + 1) (k + 1)
definitions.docstring:
**Pitman's consistency condition.**  A `k`-merger among `b` blocks is a `k`-merger among
`b+1` that misses the extra block, or a `(k+1)`-merger that includes it.  A rate array
satisfying this, and only such an array, comes from a single process compatible across
sample sizes.

hypotheses: ∀ b k, 3 ≤ k → lam b k = 0

Descent.Coalescent.binaryRate_eq_base: ∀ b k, 3 ≤ k → lam b k = 0

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.kingmanRate
definitions.docstring:
Kingman's array: binary mergers at unit rate, nothing else.  K-C (1.3) as a member of
Pitman's family.

hypotheses: ∀ b k, 3 ≤ k → lam b k = 0

Descent.Coalescent.eq_kingmanRate: ∀ b k, 3 ≤ k → lam b k = 0

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.totalRate
definitions.body: ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 2 b, (b.choose k : ℝ) * lam b k
definitions.docstring:
The total rate out of a state with `b` blocks: every `k`-subset that can merge, at its
own rate.  For Kingman this is `C(b,2)`; in general it is what
`Descent.Coalescent.StateSpace.card_covers` would count if covers allowed multiple
mergers.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.coalescentLaw
definitions.signature: (n k m : ℕ) (holdLaw : Measure ℝ) : Measure (List (ER n) × (Fin m → ℝ))
definitions.body: (chainLaw n k).toMeasure.prod (Measure.pi fun _ : Fin m => holdLaw)
definitions.docstring:
**The law of a coupled trajectory and clock.**  The jump chain's law, producted with `m` independent copies of a holding-time law.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM, and in particular the independence of the two
factors is BUILT IN rather than derived -- see the module docstring.  Kingman's Theorem 3
does the same; his Theorem 1, which derives it, is a different theorem and is not here.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.lookdownApply
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} {α : Type*} (i j : Fin n) (c : Fin n → α) : Fin n → α
definitions.body: fun l ↦ if l = j then c i else c l
definitions.docstring:
**The lookdown operation.**  Level `j` looks down at level `i` and adopts its type;
every other level is untouched.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is an assignment, written down.  Which pairs
look down when is the modelling question, and for Kingman's coalescent the answer is
independent rate-one clocks on each pair.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.moranMass
definitions.docstring: K-G (4.5): the Moran model's family-size law, as a mass function on `{0, 1, 2}`.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.mergeSetMap
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (ξ : ER n) (S : Finset (Quotient ξ)) (a : Quotient ξ) : Quotient ξ → Quotient ξ
definitions.body: fun c => if c ∈ S then a else c
definitions.docstring: Fold every block in `S` onto `a`.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.mergeSet
definitions.signature: {n : ℕ} (ξ : ER n) (S : Finset (Quotient ξ)) (a : Quotient ξ) : ER n
definitions.body: Setoid.ker fun x => mergeSetMap ξ S a (Quotient.mk ξ x)
definitions.docstring:
**Merge a whole set of blocks at once.**  The `Λ`-coalescent's move: `|S|` blocks become
one.  Written as a kernel, so it is an equivalence relation with no argument.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  It is the edge set of the multiple-merger
coalescent's transition graph, not a claim about any population.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.identityByDescent
definitions.docstring:
K-G p.34: the probability that two individuals are identical by descent, summed over the
number of generations back to their common ancestor.  The index `s` here counts from zero,
so the coalescence happens `s + 1` generations back and `2(s+1)` births are exposed to
mutation.

Empirical status: DERIVED from the mechanism, given the pair coalescence law that
`Descent.Coalescent.WrightFisher.pairDistinct_eq_pow` counts off uniform parent choice.  The
one modelling input beyond that is that mutation hits each birth independently with probability `β`.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.ewensDenominator
definitions.docstring: The rising factorial `(θ+1)(θ+2)⋯(θ+n-1)` that normalises K-G (3.8).

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.ewensProb
definitions.body:
θ ^ (Multiset.card lam - 1) / ewensDenominator θ n
    * (((lam.map fun l => (l - 1)!).prod : ℕ) : ℝ)
definitions.docstring:
**K-G (3.8).**  The probability that the allelic relation on a sample of `n` is a given
equivalence relation with class sizes `lam`.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM as written -- it is Kingman's formula.  What makes
it more than a stipulation is that it is a consequence of the coalescent plus Poisson
mutation, and that it normalises; the normalisation is checked below at `n = 2, 3`.

**K-C (3.4): the paintbox relation.**  Two balls are related when they are the same ball,
or when they carry the same colour and that colour is not the special colour `0`.  Colour `0`

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  This is a construction of equivalence relations
from colourings.

definitions.name: Descent.Coalescent.permAction

The permutation action of K-C (3.1): `π̂R` relates `x` and `y` when `R` relates their
preimages.

**K-C (3.20).**  The `𝒫_k`-probability that a sample of `n` still shows all `k` colours:

**K-G (6.5): the coalescent path of one trajectory.**  `chain k` is the state with `k`
blocks; the path reads it off at the current block count.

Empirical status: NOT AN EMPIRICAL CLAIM.  This is Kingman's construction, with the jump
chain and the holding times supplied rather than drawn -- the law is exactly what this file
does not provide.
